questions.question: According to Megasthenes, how many gates were there in Pataliputra?
questions.solution:
According to the Greek historian Megasthenes, the city of Pataliputra had 64 gates and 570 towers.
  • He described it as a large and beautiful city surrounded by a massive wooden wall.
  • Pataliputra was the strategic capital of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country.
questions.solution:
In 1940, the Muslim League passed the Lahore Resolution, demanding independent states for Muslims.
  • The resolution was moved by A.K. Fazlul Huq.
  • This demand eventually led to the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

questions.question: The Moth ki Masjid was built in the reign of ______ ruler.
questions.solution:
Moth ki Masjid was built in Delhi during the reign of Sikandar Lodi.
  • It was constructed by his Prime Minister, Miyan Bhuya.
  • The mosque is a fine example of Lodi-style architecture.

questions.question: ____________ Veda, shortest among the four Vedas, holds a divine status in Hindu tradition and is a collection of melodies and chants.
questions.solution:
The Sama Veda is the shortest of all Vedas and is considered the root of Indian classical music.
  • It consists of melodies (Samans) intended to be sung during sacrifices.
  • Most of its verses are taken from the Rig Veda.

questions.question: In 1877, Viceroy Lytton organised a Durbar to acknowledge ______ as the Empress of India.
questions.solution:
In 1877, Viceroy Lord Lytton held a grand Delhi Durbar to proclaim Queen Victoria as the 'Empress of India' (Kaiser-i-Hind).
  • This occurred during a time when parts of India were facing a severe famine.
  • The event highlighted the symbolic power of the British monarchy over India.

questions.question: In ancient times the area to the south of the_____ river was known as Magadha.
questions.solution:
In ancient times, the powerful Mahajanapada of Magadha was located to the south of the Ganga river.
  • Rivers like the Son also flowed through it, providing water and transport.
  • Its location helped it control trade and agricultural surplus.

questions.question: When was the Harijan Sewak Sangh founded as a result of the Poona Pact?
questions.solution:
The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1932.
  • It was established following the Poona Pact to work for the removal of untouchability.
  • Gandhi started the weekly journal 'Harijan' to promote these social reforms.

questions.question: Which among the following Vedas is the oldest?
questions.solution:
The Rig Veda is the oldest Veda among the four.
  • It is a collection of 1,028 hymns dedicated to Vedic deities.
  • It provides insight into the early Aryan society in India.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Law was given by ________________.
questions.solution:
The Modern Periodic Law was proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913.
  • It states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
  • This replaced Mendeleev's periodic law which was based on atomic mass.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties controlled the Silk Route during post Mauryan period?
questions.solution:
The Kushanas were the most famous dynasty to control the Silk Route in the post-Mauryan period.
  • They benefited from the taxes collected from traders passing through their territory.
  • Under King Kanishka, the empire reached its peak.

questions.question: During which movement did Chauri-Chaura incident happen?
questions.solution:
The Chauri-Chaura incident took place in 1922 during the Non-Cooperation Movement.
  • A group of protesters clashed with police, resulting in the death of 22 policemen.
  • This violence led Mahatma Gandhi to immediately call off the movement.

questions.question: Hymns of the Rigveda are known as __________.
questions.solution:
Hymns in the Rigveda are called Sukta, which literally means 'well-said'.
  • These hymns were composed by sages (Rishis) to praise various gods.
  • They were passed down orally for generations before being written.

questions.question: Which of the following Satyagraha was led by Dr. BR Ambedkar?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927.
  • The protest was held to assert the right of 'untouchables' to use water from the public Chawdar Tank.
  • It is considered one of the first significant organized protests by Dalits.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Harappan cities is called the lower city? Eastern
questions.solution:
In Harappan cities, the Eastern part was generally larger but lower, and is called the 'Lower Town'.
  • The western part was smaller but higher, known as the Citadel.
  • The Citadel usually contained important public buildings like the Great Bath.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Mauryan Empire?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BC after defeating the last Nanda king, Dhana Nanda.
  • He was assisted by his mentor and advisor, Chanakya (Kautilya).
  • He established the first great pan-Indian empire.

questions.question: Why did Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar Ul Haq resign from the Imperial Legislative Council?
questions.option_2: to protest against the Simon commission
questions.option_3: to protest against the Rowlatt Act
questions.solution:
Leaders like Jinnah and Malaviya resigned from the Council to protest against the Rowlatt Act of 1919.
  • The Act gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities.
  • It allowed the detention of political prisoners without trial for up to two years.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of Vajji Mahajanapada?
questions.solution:
Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji Mahajanapada.
  • Vajji was a confederacy of various clans, including the Lichchhavis.
  • It was governed by a system called Gana-Sangha (an early form of republic).

questions.question: Identify the Mauryan king who gave up conquest after winning a war.
questions.solution:
Ashoka is the Mauryan king who famously gave up war and conquest.
  • The turning point was the Kalinga War, where he felt deep remorse over the loss of life.
  • He then adopted the path of Dhamma (righteousness).

questions.question: When did the infamous Jallianwala Bagh incident take place?
questions.solution:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on April 13, 1919.
  • It occurred on the day of the Baisakhi festival.
  • The Hunter Commission was later appointed to investigate the incident.

questions.question: When did Ashoka, the Mauryan ruler, die?
questions.solution:
Ashoka, the Great, died in 232 BC after reigning for nearly 40 years.
  • His death was followed by a gradual decline of the Mauryan Empire.
  • The empire eventually collapsed about 50 years after his death.

questions.question: In ______, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East.
questions.solution:
In 1600, the East India Company received a Royal Charter from Queen Elizabeth I.
  • This granted the company the monopoly to trade with the East.
  • The company first arrived at the port of Surat in 1608.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to Indian in January ______.
questions.solution:
Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in January 1915.
  • His arrival is celebrated annually as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (Jan 9).
  • His first major successful satyagraha in India was in Champaran (1917).

questions.question: The Great Stupa of Sanchi was built during the reign of which of the following kings?
questions.solution:
The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Ashoka in the 3rd century BC.
  • It is one of the oldest stone structures in India and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
  • The stupa houses relics of the Buddha.

questions.question: The Prarthana Samaj was established in ______ in Bombay.
questions.solution:
The Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867 in Bombay.
  • It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj of Bengal.
  • It focused on social reforms like rational worship and the abolition of caste.

questions.question: Ruler of which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple in 999?
questions.solution:
The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple at Khajuraho was built by the Chandela dynasty.
  • It was constructed by King Dhangadeva around 999 AD.
  • The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is known for its intricate carvings.
